### Epistemological & Political Leanings

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Cross-cultural friendliness** | Medium-High — international experimental-psychology authorship |
| **Non-Western epistemology openness** | N/A — paradigm-unified experimental venue |
| **Diversity topic receptiveness** | Medium — diversity in samples encouraged |
| **Dominant theoretical tradition** | Experimental psychology of learning, memory, cognition — episodic/semantic memory, working memory, attention, categorization, decision-making, language processing |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** Yes (strong)
- **If yes, what kind?** Manuscripts must demonstrate **rigorous experimental methodology** in learning, memory, or cognition domains. Multi-experiment programmatic designs strongly preferred.
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Single-experiment designs face skepticism. Manuscripts outside learning/memory/cognition scope redirected to other JEP titles.

| Quantitative experimental | 5 | Core method — controlled lab experiments on memory/cognition |
| Qualitative interviews | 0 | Outside scope |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Outside scope |
| Theoretical / Conceptual | 3 | Theoretical work when bridging to experimental evidence |
| Mixed methods | 1 | Outside scope |
| Meta-analysis | 4 | Welcomed in memory / cognition literatures |
| Computational modeling | 5 | Distinctive strength — memory/cognition models (e.g., REM, SAM, SIMPLE, ACT-R) |

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

Reviewers drawn primarily from APA Division 3 (Experimental Psychology) and Psychonomic Society networks. Expect deep literacy in memory models, attention research, categorization, decision-making, language processing. Common reviewer demands: "Multi-experiment replication?", "Theoretical contribution beyond effect demonstration?", "Computational model fit?".

## Strategic Notes

### Hard Blockers

- Manuscripts outside learning / memory / cognition scope
- Pure qualitative submissions
- Single-experiment designs without strong theoretical justification
- Failure to disclose AI use per APA publisher policy

### Soft Tax

Low for experimental memory/cognition tradition authors. APA-style formatting standard; multi-experiment programs preferred. Long APA review cycle should be expected.

### Best Suited For

- Memory mechanism empirical studies (episodic, semantic, working, autobiographical)
- Attention and cognitive control experiments
- Categorization and concept research
- Decision-making and reasoning experiments
- Language processing studies
- Computational modeling of memory/cognition (REM, SAM, ACT-R, etc.)
- Multi-experiment programmatic memory research

### Not Recommended For

- Perception-focused work (consider JEP:HPP)
- Cognitive psychology with broad scope (consider JEP:General)
- Applied cognition (consider JEP:Applied)
- Pure qualitative or first-person work
- Neuropsychology with clinical-population focus

### Rejection Fallback Chain

| Rank | Journal | Why this fallback works |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Journal of Experimental Psychology General](./journal-of-experimental-psychology-general.md) | If broader-experimental scope; APA family |
| 2 | [Cognitive Psychology](./cognitive-psychology.md) | If theoretical-cognitive contribution; Elsevier |
| 3 | [Cognition](./cognition.md) | If cognitive theoretical advance; Elsevier |

**Reverse direction** *(optional)*: If your paper was rejected from JEP:General as "too memory-specialized," JEP:LMC is the better-fit subfield specialist within the APA JEP family — same paradigm, sharper memory/cognition expertise.
